'''Gillian Lesley Slater''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FIMA}} (née Filtness) is a retired British mathematician and academic administrator, the former [[vice chancellor]] of [[Bournemouth University]].{{r|wow}}

==Education==
Slater read mathematics in [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]], where she served as secretary of the [[Oxford University Liberal Democrats]] in 1969.{{r|ould}} She completed a DPhil at the [[University of Oxford]] in 1973, with the dissertation ''Some Topics in Functional–Differential Equations'' supervised by [[John Bryce McLeod]].{{r|mg|diss}}

==Career==
Slater became a mathematics instructor at South Bank Polytechnic (now [[London South Bank University]]) and at Sheffield City Polytechnic (now [[Sheffield Hallam University]]). She moved into academic administration as dean of science and technology at Manchester Polytechnic, and then after it became [[Manchester Metropolitan University]], as pro-vice-chancellor.{{r|wow}}

Her next step was to become vice chancellor of [[Bournemouth University]], in 1994,{{r|top}} succeeding the university's first vice chancellor, Bernard MacManus.{{r|macmanus}} She came under pressure from the UK's Labour government in 2004 for taking a stand against the government's push to institute differential fees for different universities,{{r|parapet}} and retired in 2005, replaced as vice chancellor by atmospheric scientist Paul Curran.{{r|curran}}
